title: Pivot a tableau

blocks.text: The pump-scheduling simplex now knows where to pivot. It needs the step itself: rewrite the tableau so the entering variable becomes basic in the leaving row, which moves the plan to a neighbouring vertex.

Write `pivot(T, r, k)` in `pivot.py`. `T` is a tableau (constraint rows, then the objective row; every row ends with its right-hand side), `r` the pivot row and `k` the pivot column, with $`T_{r,k} \neq 0`$. Return a new tableau $`T'`$ with

T'_{r,j} = \frac{T_{r,j}}{T_{r,k}} \quad \forall j, \qquad
T'_{i,j} = T_{i,j} - T_{i,k}\, T'_{r,j} \quad \forall i \neq r,\ \forall j
where $`i`$ runs over every row, the objective row included, and $`j`$ over every column, the right-hand side included. After it, column $`k`$ is 1 in row $`r`$ and 0 in every other row.
Leave `T` unchanged: the caller keeps the old tableau to print it next to the new one.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from pivot import pivot

T = [[2, 1, 1, 0, 0, 10],
     [1, 2, 0, 1, 0, 8],
     [0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 3],
     [-4, -5, 0, 0, 0, 0]]
after = pivot(T, 2, 1)
for i, row in enumerate(after):
    print(f"row {i} after pivot (2, 1):", [round(v, 4) for v in row])
print("row 3 of T itself:", T[3])

from __future__ import annotations


def pivot(T: list[list[float]], r: int, k: int) -> list[list[float]]:
    """The tableau after pivoting on row r and column k. T itself is left unchanged."""
    # TODO: divide row r by T[r][k]; from every other row i, objective row included, subtract
    # T[i][k] times the new row r. Build a new tableau rather than changing T.
    return [list(row) for row in T]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    T = [[1, 1, 1, 0, 5],
         [2, 1, 0, 1, 8],
         [-3, -2, 0, 0, 0]]
    for row in pivot(T, 1, 0):
        print(row)

cases.says: after the pivot the column is 1 in the pivot row and 0 in the other constraint rows
a pivot element other than 1 divides its whole row, right-hand side included
the objective row is cleared in the pivot column too, so its last entry is the new value
the function returns a new tableau and leaves the one it was given as it was

origin.section: A Pivot Rewrites the Tableau So the Entering Variable Is Basic

concepts: a vertex is a basic feasible solution: n variables at zero and the rest solved from the equations
a pivot divides the pivot row and clears the column from every other row, objective included
